claims.head: Iron sharpens iron
claims.body: The Oilers are near the top of the league for chance quality, but the Kraken are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. We think the Kraken win this one.
claims.call: The Kraken keep the Oilers’ chances less dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot).
claims.nums: Edmonton 7th for chance quality (a 6.5% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Seattle 3rd for preventing dangerous shots

claims.head: The Kraken can’t afford to take penalties
claims.call: The Oilers’ power play creates at least their usual 9.9 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Oilers’ power play is the league’s best, and the Kraken’s kill is one of the worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Kraken more than most. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.

EDM.head: A big edge for the Oilers
EDM.body: Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Kraken’s best way in is getting good looks.

SEA.head: The Oilers should be favored
SEA.body: Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. To pull this off, the Kraken can start with getting good looks, plus Joey Daccord stealing the show.

story.head: Draisaitl’s favorite opponent
paras: The Kraken come in at 1-0-0, the Oilers at 1-0-1.

items.text: Leon Draisaitl has a point in eight straight games against Seattle, and 19 points in his last nine against them.
Bobby McMann has six goals in seven games against Edmonton since 2023-24, most of them with Toronto.
The Oilers have been without Zach Hyman, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Matt Savoie all season.
Joey Daccord has never won in Edmonton: he is 0-7-1 there in his career.
